How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, JANUARY 23, 2024
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the special meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:33 p.m. on
Tuesday, January 23, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Khan.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Viki Goto, Riaz (Rick) Khan, and Chasity
  Jennings-Nuñez

Commissioners Absent:  Cathie Chavez-Morris, George Herrera-Avila

Youth Ambassadors:  Kelly Munoz Rios and Aaron Situ were both absent.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  The agenda order was approved.

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. AB 481 (MILITARY ACQUISITION, USE AND REPORTING) COMMUNITY
  PRESENTATION
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez introduced the item.

  San Gabriel Police Lieutenant Rene Lopez provided a presentation about AB 481.

  The Commission thanked Lieutenant Lopez for the presentation. Commissioners
  had questions regarding the audit and their rescue armored vehicle. They
  commented that the term “military equipment” might alarm ordinary citizens. The
  Commission also expressed that the information about policy 707 is difficult to find
  on the city’s website.

  Public comment by Andrew, a resident, has an issue with the policy, section 770
  subsection D. He also requested additions to the city’s policy.

  B. ALL ARE WELCOME PROGRAM FINAL UPDATE
  Presented by Manager Morales-Stevens.

  The Commissioners are working to identify the businesses that will be a part of
  the pilot program. They discussed the launch strategy, and budget and provided
  edits to the webpage.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  JANUARY 23, 2024
   C. DISCUSSION OF PROPOSED LINKAGE/ RESOURCE SERVICES
  Presented by Manager Morales-Stevens.

  The Commissioners provided feedback, suggesting that this program stays
  focused on mental health services. They inquired about helping those who speak
  various languages and recommended using translation services.

  Public Comment: None

  D. DISCUSSION ON APPROVED 2024 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Jennings-Nuñez

  The Commission spoke about the youth ambassadors’ interviews and timeline.
  They requested that the interview date be included in the application. There will
  be changes to the interview process.

  Commissioners proposed forming a committee to regularly connect with the
  police department.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Vice-Chair Goto shared that the commissioners along with city staff toured the Japanese
  American National Museum’s The Bias Inside Us exhibit. She recognized that February is
  Black History Month and provided film suggestions, American Fiction, and Rustin.

  Commissioner Khan shared his experience attending The Bias Inside Us exhibit.

  Commissioner Brenhaug also talked about her experience at the exhibit and appreciated
  their discussion after the tour.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez thanked Vice Chair Goto for arranging the tour and thanked the
  staff for attending. She announced that it was National Maternal Health Awareness Day.
  She encouraged people to speak to their legislators regarding the clinics that are closing
  every day which provide care to women and birthing people. Chair Jennings-Nuñez will
  host an art exhibit at Blossom Market again this February. She thanked Commissioner Khan
  for his service on the HEAR Commission, this is his last meeting. She also acknowledged
  that it was Commissioner Herrera-Avila’s final meeting.

  Commissioner Khan appreciated the members for their understanding and his positive
  experience as a first-time commission member.

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  All Are Welcome Program Update

INTRODUCTION

Staff have worked closely with the HEAR Commission members to create a Citywide All Are
Welcome program. Presented in the report is an outline of the program including the purpose,
how it will work and how it will be evaluated. The program is not expected to have a termination
date. However, staff will provide updates to council on the success of the program in terms of
participating agencies and feedback from residents and businesses. Staff estimates the costs to
create an educational video, advertise the program and create print materials for the program at
$1,500.

ANALYSIS

Purpose
The purpose of the program is to emphasize inclusive and welcoming areas within the City of
San Gabriel where people can feel comfortable being their authentic selves regardless of their
sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression. The highlighted space is also expected
to be free of aggression, judgment and hate.

The program falls in alignment with and contributes to the progress of the City’s Vision
statement. The vision statement reads, “Building on its rich history, San Gabriel will stand out as
a vibrant, inclusive and inviting place to live work, shop, and play. San Gabriel will set the
standard for excellence and innovation.”

Process
  1. Organizations that are interested in participating in the All Are Welcome program will
  review the program information posted on the City website and complete the
  participation request form.
  2. Once staff receive the form a sticker will be mailed out to the organization so they may
  display it on their front window or other immediately visible location to the public.
   All Are Welcome Update
  January 23, 2024
  Page 2

  a. In addition to the sticker participating organizations will receive a custom video
  from the HEAR Commission reminding them of the purpose of the program and
  educational information about the community they are committing to create a
  safe space for. The program may be offered in partnership with the SGV LGBTQ
  Center. Details are still being finalized by staff and the committee.
  3. The participating organization will continue to foster an inclusive and welcoming space
  for all who enter.

The program will be evaluated in a year to determine the following:
  • Number of participating organizations
  • Response from the San Gabriel Community
  • Response from participating organizations
  o A short survey will be sent out to participating agencies via survey monkey

Staff will work with the Economic Development Department to share the program with local
businesses. All businesses and organizations would be informed of the program, but
participation is optional.

Proposed Symbol to Be Prominently Displayed at Organizations:

RECCOMENDATION

The program information was approved at the June 27, 2023 HEAR Commission meeting.
However, the program committee is looking for direction and support from the
Commission. Staff anticipate presenting the item to City Council at the February 20, 2024
Council meeting. Should it be approved the Committee will need the Commission’s
support in securing 10-15 organizations to commit to the program before a full launch of
the program to the public in June.

Staff recommend the Commission agree to the commitment of garnering support from
local businesses prior to a full launch. If the Commission is unable to provide the time
needed leading up to the June launch, staff recommend pushing back the launch of the
program.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  January 23, 2024

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2024 Approved Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
Commission and is intended for the 2024 calendar year. The 2024 Annual Workplan was
approved by the City Council during the April 18, 2023 Council meeting.

Purpose of the Commission
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.

Scope of the Commission
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan presented is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission
and outline the areas of focus for the remainder of 2024. It includes proposed programs
and projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year, some of which
may extend beyond 2024. Some of the items identified have carried over from the 2023
workplan.
   HEAR Commission 2024 Approved Annual Workplan
  January 23, 2024
  Page 2

APPROVED 2023 WORKPLAN
The 2024 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission has
identified as key areas of interest in furthering its purpose. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

  1. Equity Training in City Policies (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Equity)
  a. Request an update from the Human Resources Department during a regular
  HEAR Commission meeting pertaining to a policy for Implicit Bias training
  requirements for City employees and staff. The update should include how
  often the training occurs and the focus of the training.
  b. Provide annual training for HEAR Commission members, including youth
  ambassadors, and staff through an organization such as the Government
  Alliance on Race and Equity (GARE).

  2. Community Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Diversity, Mutual Appreciation and Increased Cultural Competency)
  a. Develop and implement programs and events that engage and educate the
  community to promote the goals of the HEAR Commission.
  i. Examples include:
  1. Continue providing programs and services for Mental
  Wellness, including, but not limited to, a movie screening with
  a panel discussion in May.
  2. Youth Ambassadors to lead project to engage local youth.
  3. Develop and implement the All Are Welcome Program and
  create a PRIDE event in support of the SGV LGBTQ Center’s
  Pride Tour.
  b. Ensure the City continues to recognize Native American Heritage Month and
  Black History Month, at a minimum by proclamation, with the hopes of
  expansion.
  c. Guest speaker(s)/educational program(s) during the regular Commission
  meetings (one per month) which relate to the scope of the Commission.
  i. Examples include: Bystander Training, anti-bias training, cultural
  diversity, mental-health awareness, climate change, affordable
  housing, homelessness and other relevant topics.
  d. Develop and implement an active community member award from the
  HEAR Commission.
   HEAR Commission 2024 Approved Annual Workplan
  January 23, 2024
  Page 3

  e. Recommend to City Council that the City implement a multicultural event/
  celebration that could be done in conjunction with the City’s birthday
  celebration.
  f. Conduct community outreach at meetings or events hosted by local
  community groups to increase awareness and engagement.

3. Youth Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Diversity
  and Access)
  a. Continue the Youth Ambassador program - applications for 2024 will open
  in January 2024.
  b. Recommend other City commissions and departments to develop a youth
  leadership/internship opportunity.
  c. Promote and/or develop youth internship opportunities, including, but not
  limited to, a Social Media internship.

4. Community Information (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Access)
  a. Recommend to the City Council that the HEAR Commission receive the first
  draft of plans to implement additional services pertaining to mental health.
  b. Implement and ensure a more accessible and centralized resource page is
  available on the City website on various topics relating to the scope of the
  Commission.
  c. Implement a fraud/cybersecurity seminar, potentially through the San
  Gabriel Police Department.

5. Accessibility (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Access)
  a. Determine various forms of outreach specifically for persons whose primary
  language is not English to ensure meetings and activities are accessible.
  b. Enhance access to community events and activities for persons with a
  disability.

6. Partnerships (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Increased cultural
  competence and positive inter-group relations)
  a. Partner with the Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission
  to pay tribute to the indigenous peoples of San Gabriel at Smith Park-
  specifically the passive area on the western side of the park.
  b. Meet with the SGPD to partner on improved community policing strategies,
  especially in relation to residents who are neurodivergent and those with
  mental illness.

7. Data Collection (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Equity and
  Diversity)
  a. Invite San Gabriel Police Chief Edward Elizalde to a commission meeting to
  provide information on the community policing program and the results of
  the Racial and Identity Profiling Advisory Report.
  b. Ensure the City’s data collections efforts through community surveys and
  summary data results are translated into Chinese, Spanish, and Vietnamese
  for equitable access. An example is the budget surplus survey.
